inlines.text: Your friend currently earns $119,000 a year. She is about to get a $3000 pay rise.
In which tax bracket is she in currently?

answer.worked: \$119,000 lies in the third bracket, \$45,001–\$120,000. Its marginal tax rate is 32.5%.

inlines.text: In which tax bracket will she be in afterwards?

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\text{New income}&=119\,000+3000\\&=\$122\,000\end{align*}$
\$122,000 lies in the fourth bracket, \$120,001–\$180,000. Its marginal tax rate is 37%.

inlines.text: Your friend says: “I don’t want the pay rise. The government will start taxing me at 37%, rather than 32.5%, which means I’ll have less money than before!”
Explain to your friend why she is incorrect, using mathematical reasoning:

answer.short: Third bracket; excess \$74,000; tax \$29,142; after-tax income \$89,858.
answer.worked:
Third tax bracket.
$\begin{align*}\text{Excess}&=119\,000-45\,000\\&=\$74\,000\\\text{Tax payable}&=5092+0.325\times74\,000\\&=\$29\,142\\\text{After-tax income}&=119\,000-29\,142\\&=\$89\,858\end{align*}$

answer.short: Income \$122,000; fourth bracket; excess \$2000; tax \$30,207; after-tax income \$91,793.
answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\text{New income}&=119\,000+3000\\&=\$122\,000\end{align*}$
Fourth tax bracket.
$\begin{align*}\text{Excess}&=122\,000-120\,000\\&=\$2000\\\text{Tax payable}&=29\,467+0.37\times2000\\&=\$30\,207\\\text{After-tax income}&=122\,000-30\,207\\&=\$91\,793\end{align*}$

inlines.text: The new tax rate is only on each

answer.short: Additional. Only income above \$120,000 is taxed at 37%; her after-tax income increases by \$1935.
answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\text{Increase in after-tax income}&=91\,793-89\,858\\&=\$1935\end{align*}$
She has more money after the pay rise. The first \$1000 of the rise is taxed at 32.5%, and the remaining \$2000 is taxed at 37%. The 37% rate applies only to additional dollars above \$120,000; it does not apply to her whole income.

content.prompt:
Shirley makes \$30 an hour and works 35 hours a week. She has tax deductions totalling \$550.
She has paid fortnightly tax instalments of \$200. Calculate her tax refund or liability.

answer.worked:
Using 52 weeks and 26 fortnights per year:
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Gross income} &= 30\times35\times52\\
\text{Gross income} &= \$54\,600\\
\text{Taxable income} &= 54\,600-550\\
\text{Taxable income} &= \$54\,050\\
\text{Excess} &= 54\,050-45\,000\\
\text{Excess} &= \$9050\\
\text{Tax payable} &= 5092+0.325\times9050\\
\text{Tax payable} &= \$8033.25\\
\text{Total instalments} &= 200\times26\\
\text{Total instalments} &= \$5200\\
\text{Refund/liability balance} &= 5200-8033.25\\
\text{Refund/liability balance} &= -\$2833.25
\end{align*}$$
Shirley has paid too little tax, so she has a tax liability of \$2833.25.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Gross income} &= 989.60\times52 = \$51\,459.20\\\text{Deductions} &= 38.25\times52+150 = \$2\,139\\\text{Taxable income before rounding} &= 51\,459.20-2\,139 = \$49\,320.20\\\text{Taxable income} &= \$49\,320\quad\text{(rounded down)}\end{align*}$$
The taxable income is in the \$45,001–\$120,000 bracket.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Income tax} &= 5\,092+0.325\times(49\,320-45\,000)\\\text{Income tax} &= \$6\,496.00\\\text{Medicare levy} &= 0.02\times49\,320 = \$986.40\\\text{Total tax payable} &= 6\,496.00+986.40 = \$7\,482.40\\\text{Annual PAYG} &= 229.02\times52 = \$11\,909.04\\\text{Refund} &= 11\,909.04-7\,482.40 = \$4\,426.64\end{align*}$$
PAYG exceeds total tax payable, so Liam receives a tax refund.

content.prompt:
Gabby is an Australian resident who earned a yearly salary of \$204 560. She claimed tax deductions of \$10 534 and paid a total of \$72 156 PAYG tax.

Calculate her tax liability or refund, if she has to pay the Medicare levy.

Use the supplied 2022–23 resident tax table and a 2% Medicare levy. Round taxable income down to whole dollars and each completed income-tax and Medicare levy amount to cents before calculating total tax.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Taxable income} &= 204\,560-10\,534=\$194\,026\\
\text{Excess} &= 194\,026-180\,000=\$14\,026\\
\text{Income tax} &= 51\,667+0.45\times14\,026\\
\text{Income tax} &= \$57\,978.70\\
\text{Medicare levy} &= 0.02\times194\,026=\$3\,880.52\\
\text{Total tax payable} &= 57\,978.70+3\,880.52=\$61\,859.22\\
\text{Refund} &= 72\,156-61\,859.22=\$10\,296.78
\end{align*}$$
Her PAYG payments exceed her total tax payable, so she receives a refund.

inlines.text: Last year, Luke’s taxable income was $34 000.
This year, Luke’s taxable income has increased by $16 800.
How much extra money will Luke have this year, after paying tax, as a result of the increase in his taxable income?

answer.worked:
Last year, Luke was in the second tax bracket.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Excess}&=34\,000-18\,200\\\text{Excess}&=15\,800\\\text{Tax payable}&=0+0.19\times15\,800\\\text{Tax payable}&=\$3\,002\\\text{After-tax income}&=34\,000-3\,002\\\text{After-tax income}&=\$30\,998\end{align*}$$
This year, his taxable income is $34\,000+16\,800=\$50\,800$, in the third tax bracket.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Excess}&=50\,800-45\,000\\\text{Excess}&=5\,800\\\text{Tax payable}&=5\,092+0.325\times5\,800\\\text{Tax payable}&=\$6\,977\\\text{After-tax income}&=50\,800-6\,977\\\text{After-tax income}&=\$43\,823\\\text{Extra after-tax income}&=43\,823-30\,998\\\text{Extra after-tax income}&=\$12\,825\end{align*}$$

entries.description:
1 year = 12 months (per annum p.a. means per year)
= 52 weeks
= 26 fortnights

When converting to a larger unit, we divide, since we will need fewer units.
When converting to a smaller unit, we multiply, since we will need more units.

Note that these are close estimates;
A non-leap year has 365 days, but 52 weeks would only have 364 days.

A common misconception is treating four weeks as a month.
This is not true. Four weeks is 28 days. Only February has 28 days.
